preamble: Reduction of [o] to [ə] is a common outcome of stress-driven vowel reduction: in unstressed syllables the vowel loses its rounding and backness and centralizes. Russian reduces unstressed /o/ to [ə] outside the immediately pretonic syllable, English alternates full and reduced vowels between related words (photo vs photography), and Neapolitan neutralized final unstressed /a/, /e/, /o/ to [ə].

examples.note: When stress shifts to the second syllable, the first-syllable o reduces to [ə].
Final unstressed /o/ is weakened to schwa, merging with final /a/ and /e/ (longa [ˈloŋɡə]).

sources: Wikipedia contributors. Vowel reduction in Russian. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vowel_reduction_in_Russian
context: In unstressed syllables; reduction is conditioned by stress placement
allophones_note: In Russian: unstressed /o/ outside the pretonic syllable is realized [ə]; in English: unstressed syllables; in Neapolitan: word-final unstressed position
